# Rule sheet

*Generated by `scratch/rules/build_rule_sheet.py` from `config/rules.yaml` and `config/rule_sheet_text.en.yaml`. Do not edit by hand: change the rules or the wording, then regenerate.*

Rules version: `rules-v1.7-2026-11-16`. 63 flags: 38 Attention, 2 Return, 23 Info.

## What the system does and does not do

The system reads each carrier explanation, turns it into line items, checks the result and raises flags. **It never decides whether a charge is justified or should be paid.** Every record goes to a reviewer, whatever its colour. The buttons on the review screen only record the reviewer's own decision. The model is never told how its reading compares with any amount in the Excel row (Delta, invoice amount); those amounts are used only to evaluate the system.

## How the colour of a record is decided

The colour is computed from the flags of the record, in this order. It is never computed from how confident the model says it is.

1. If any flag has severity **Attention**: **Human review**.
2. Otherwise, if any flag has severity **Return**: **Return suggested**.
3. Otherwise: **Passed checks**.

**Info** flags are shown to the reviewer and never change the colour. "Passed checks" means the reading passed the checks and has no flag a person must look at. It does not mean the reading is correct or the charge is payable.

A **return** is suggested only where code alone can decide: empty text, or text with numbers but no letters. Anything that depends on the model's reading goes to a person, because keeping a correct claim out of the process is the worst failure.

### Flags shown as Info when another flag already explains them

When one of the flags on the right is present on a record, the flag on the left is shown as Info, because the flag on the right is decided by code alone and already implies it.

| Flag | Shown as Info when this is present |
|---|---|
| `ITEM.AMOUNT.UNNAMED` | `REC.TEXT.NUMBERS_ONLY` |

## The flags

Severity: Attention = a person must look; Return = a return to the carrier can be suggested; Info = shown only.

### The text of the note

| Flag | Severity | When it is raised | What to look at |
|---|---|---|---|
| `REC.TEXT.EMPTY` | Return | The carrier's explanation is empty or only spaces. | Nothing to read. A return to the carrier can be suggested, asking for each charge and its amount. Wording in a return draft: "Add an explanation naming each charge and its amount." |
| `REC.TEXT.NUMBERS_ONLY` | Return | The explanation has digits but no letters at all (for example just "126.50"). | The amount has no charge name. A return can be suggested, asking which charge each amount is for. Wording in a return draft: "Name the charge each amount is for, and why it applies." |
| `REC.TEXT.NO_NUMBER` | Attention | The explanation has words but no number at all. | A charge is named without an amount, so it cannot be checked against the invoice adjustment. A claim may still be valid, so a person looks. |
| `REC.TEXT.INJECTION_SUSPECT` | Attention | The text matches a pattern that looks like an instruction to the model (for example "ignore previous instructions"), or contains unprintable characters, or is very long. | Read the original text. The text may be trying to influence the automatic processing. The model is told to treat note text as data only. |
| `REC.TEXT.SCREEN_ADDRESSED_TO_SYSTEM` | Attention | A separate screening call, which sees only the text, says the text speaks to an AI system, a model, a tool or the review process. The quoted words must appear in the text. | Read the quote in the original text. The screening never changes the reading and never skips it; a person decides whether the text is an attempt to steer the system. |
| `REC.TEXT.PII_REDACTED` | Info | A personal name or e-mail address was replaced by a placeholder before the text went to the model. | Nothing to do. Shown so that the reviewer knows the text on screen was changed. |
| `REC.TEXT.REDACTION_ALTERED_DIGITS` | Attention | The digits in the text were different before and after redaction. | Redaction may have damaged an amount, so the reading cannot be trusted. Check the original text. |
| `REC.TEXT.DATE_AFTER_EVENT` | Info | A date with a year in the text is more than the allowed number of days after the event date of the record. | The text may have been written or edited later than the event date, which matters when comparing with earlier records. |
| `REC.TEXT.NON_ASCII` | Info | The text contains characters outside plain ASCII. | Kept apart from injection detection; shown so that odd characters are not missed. |

### The other fields of the record

| Flag | Severity | When it is raised | What to look at |
|---|---|---|---|
| `REC.FIELD.CROSS_BORDER` | Info | Origin and destination are in different countries. | Tax and currency rules may differ. The currency of such a record is not derived. |
| `REC.FIELD.REASON_CODE_CONFLICT` | Info | The Reason Code of the record maps to a specific charge category and the charge code the model chose is in a different specific category. | The structured code and the text disagree. The text is the reference; the conflict is kept for statistics. |

### Numbers found in the text

| Flag | Severity | When it is raised | What to look at |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NUM.PARSE.UNRECOGNIZED_REGION` | Info | Some digits in the text were not recognised as a number or a date by the number rules (for example "CV19"). | The model read that part; its reading was compared digit by digit with the original. |
| `NUM.PARSE.SPACE_MERGED` | Info | A number was formed by joining digit groups separated by spaces (for example "1 684.68"). | The joining is a guess. It may really be two numbers. |
| `NUM.PARSE.UNUSUAL_DECIMALS` | Info | A number has a number of decimals other than 0, 1 or 2 (for example "33.744"). | The dot may be a thousands separator. |
| `NUM.PARSE.LEADING_DOT` | Info | A decimal is written starting with a dot (for example ".73"). | Often a rate such as a per-mile fuel rate, not an amount of money. |
| `NUM.PARSE.MINUS_ADJACENT` | Info | A minus sign touches a number or a dollar sign (for example "-250"). | The minus may be a negative sign or just a separator. |
| `NUM.READ.REGION_VALUE_DERIVED` | Info | Code took a value for a region it could not parse, so that a number could still be used. | Shown so that a wrong guess about a decimal point would be visible. |
| `NUM.JUDGMENT.DOLLAR_EXCLUDED` | Info | A number written with a dollar sign was not counted as part of this claim. | Check that leaving it out is justified; the words the model quoted as the reason are shown. Per-unit prices written with "@", "AT", "EACH" or "PER" do not raise this. |
| `NUM.JUDGMENT.EXCLUSION_BASIS_UNLISTED` | Attention | A dollar amount was left out of the claim, but the words the model quoted contain none of the accepted reasons listed under "Words accepted as a reason to leave an amount out" below. | The exclusion has no recognised wording behind it. Check the original text. |
| `NUM.JUDGMENT.SPACE_MERGED_IN_CLAIM` | Attention | A number formed by joining space-separated digit groups was counted in the claim. | The counted amount rests on a guess about the joining. Check the original text. |
| `NUM.JUDGMENT.CREDIT_MARK_NOT_CREDIT` | Attention | The model counted an amount as a charge, but the text next to it has a credit word or parentheses. | The amount may be a credit that was read as a charge. Check the sign of this amount in the text. |
| `NUM.JUDGMENT.CREDIT_MINUS_UNCLEAR` | Attention | A minus sign is written directly before a counted amount, with no credit word or parentheses to explain it. | The text does not say whether the minus is a separator or a credit. A person decides, whichever way the model read it. |
| `NUM.ARITH.CUE_WITHOUT_RELATION` | Info | The text has a sign of arithmetic ("@", "X", "PER", "EACH", "DAYS" and similar) but the model stated no calculation. | Possible quantity times rate that was not linked. |

### Line items (charge, amount, tax, basis)

| Flag | Severity | When it is raised | What to look at |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ITEM.ARITH.QTY_RATE_NO_RESULT` | Attention | The text gives a quantity and a rate (for example "3 DAYS @ $75") but no result. | It is not stated whether the amount is the price per unit or the whole charge. |
| `ITEM.CODE.OTHER` | Attention | The model chose the code OTHER because the charge is not in the charge-code table. | Confirm the charge name. Also a candidate for adding to the code table. |
| `ITEM.CODE.PENDING_MEANING` | Info | The charge belongs to a family whose meaning has not been confirmed with the client (for example "purchased transportation surcharge"). | The reading only says that the carrier charged this item. It does not explain what it is. |
| `ITEM.CODE.COMBINED` | Info | One amount was assigned to several charge codes. | The amount cannot be split between the charges. Do not split it by habit. |
| `ITEM.AMOUNT.MISSING` | Attention | A charge other than tax is named but has no amount. | This charge cannot be reconciled. Raised from the model's reading, so it is never a return. |
| `ITEM.AMOUNT.LEADING_DOT_COUNTED` | Attention | A counted amount is written with a leading dot, such as ".74". | Such a number may be a rate (per mile, per pound) and not an amount. No rule decides which; check the text. |
| `ITEM.AMOUNT.UNNAMED` | Attention | An amount counted in the claim has no charge code. | The text does not say what the money is for. Do not fill the name in from the Reason Code or from habit. |
| `ITEM.TAX.PRESENT` | Info | The text mentions tax of any kind. | Every tax question goes to a person, because the tax rules are not confirmed with the client. |
| `ITEM.TAX.NO_AMOUNT` | Attention | The text names a tax (for example "+ HST") but gives no tax amount. | The tax amount is not in the text. The expected tax from the table of provincial rates is shown as a hint only; it is not an amount from the text and is not added to anything. |
| `ITEM.TAX.RATE_MISMATCH` | Info | The tax amount (written or inferred) differs from base times the table rate by more than the tolerance. | Shown as a fact, never as a carrier error. Check the province and the base. |
| `ITEM.TAX.NO_RULE` | Info | Tax is mentioned but there is no rate rule for the province (not Canadian, or the table has no entry for the date). | The tax amount was not checked. |
| `ITEM.BASIS.PPG_CLAIMED` | Info | The carrier says that PPG notified, approved or listed the charge. | Not verified by the system. Check PPG's own records. |
| `ITEM.BASIS.CONTRACT_CLAIMED` | Info | The carrier cites a contract, tariff or shipping document as the basis for the charge. | Not verified by the system. Check the contract, rate sheet or document. |
| `ITEM.NATURE.RATE_CORRECTION` | Info | The charge is a correction of a rate or of how the charge was calculated. | The amount is a difference, and the contract is needed to verify it. |
| `ITEM.ARITH.RELATION_FAILS` | Attention | A calculation written in the text (a sum or a quantity times rate) does not hold when code recomputes it. | The arithmetic in the carrier's own text is wrong, or the model linked the wrong numbers. |

### The claim: what the reading counts

| Flag | Severity | When it is raised | What to look at |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CLAIM.NOTHING_COUNTED` | Attention | The text has at least one money amount and the reading counts none of them. | Often the text mentions an earlier charge without saying whether it is still asked for. A person decides. |
| `CLAIM.EARLIER_CLAIM_MENTIONED` | Attention | The reading quotes words in the text that mention an earlier claim for this shipment. | Check whether the earlier claim is still being asked for. The system does not decide this. |
| `CLAIM.ATTEMPT.STATUS_CHANGED` | Attention | Between the first and the final attempt, a number changed its kind or its status (for example from claimed to paid). | See exactly what changed and why the model gave for the change. |
| `CLAIM.RECON.TOTAL_MISMATCH` | Attention | A total stated in the text does not equal the sum of the counted amounts (plus any inferred tax). | The text's own arithmetic does not hold. |

### Copies and the shipment roll-up

| Flag | Severity | When it is raised | What to look at |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SHIP.COPY.SAME_OR_NO_PK` | Attention | One explanation appears on several rows and some of those rows have no PK or repeat a PK. | The rows may be exported copies of one explanation, or the same explanation submitted again. The PK values are not enough to tell. |
| `SHIP.ROLLUP.SUPERSEDED_SAME_CHARGE` | Attention | A later explanation on the same shipment has a line with the same charge as an earlier counted line. | By default the later line replaces the earlier one in the shipment total. Check that it is a correction and not a second charge of the same kind. |
| `SHIP.ROLLUP.SAME_AMOUNT_EARLIER` | Attention | A line has the same amount as an earlier counted line but a different charge. | By default both are added. The total with the amount counted once is shown next to it. Check which is right. |
| `SHIP.ROLLUP.RATIO_SUPERSEDED` | Attention | An amount is 1.03 to 1.07 times an earlier amount, in a text with BALANCE DUE or in the next explanation, so it looks like a restated amount. | By default only the later amount counts. Check that this is a restatement and not a second charge. |
| `SHIP.ROLLUP.BALANCE_DUE_UNRESOLVED` | Attention | The text has BALANCE DUE next to other dollar amounts and none of the known patterns explains how they relate. | The model's reading stands. Check what the balance due amount is meant to cover. |
| `SHIP.ROLLUP.BALANCE_DUE_READING_DIFFERS` | Attention | Code decides from the BALANCE DUE wording which amounts count, and the model counted something else. | The model's reading is kept and the difference is shown. Check which amounts the text asks for. |
| `SHIP.ROLLUP.TAX_PARTLY_ORPHANED` | Attention | Some but not all lines of an explanation were replaced by a later explanation, so its tax stays. | The tax may belong to the replaced lines. Check whether the tax still applies. |
| `SHIP.ROLLUP.RELATION_UNDECIDED` | Attention | Code cannot decide whether one line replaces another, for example a free-text charge on either side, an amount with no charge name, or one amount for several overlapping charges. | By default both are added. Decide whether one replaces the other. |
| `SHIP.ROLLUP.INCOMPLETE` | Attention | An explanation on the shipment has no usable reading. | The default shipment total leaves that explanation out, so the total is not complete. |
| `SHIP.GAP.NONZERO` | Info | A text states an amount due, and it differs from the total of the counted amounts. | Shown for information. The gap is never a line and never changes a total. |
| `SHIP.GAP.MULTI_EXPLANATION` | Info | The shipment has several explanations and at least one states an amount due. | Shown for information. The shipment-level stated amount and gap are left empty because the system cannot tell which explanations the stated amount covers. |
| `SHIP.ROLLUP.ECHO_OF_HISTORY_AMOUNT` | Attention | A later counted amount equals, or is 1.03 to 1.07 times, an amount an earlier explanation read as history. | The earlier reading may have missed a claim that the later explanation restates. No total changes. |
| `SHIP.ROLLUP.ORDER_TIED` | Attention | Two explanations have the same Event Date, so which is earlier rests on the row order. | A replacement between them depends on that order. Check that the direction is right. |

### The model run itself

| Flag | Severity | When it is raised | What to look at |
|---|---|---|---|
| `RUN.SCREEN.FAILED` | Attention | The screening call gave no usable answer. | The text was not screened for instructions to the system. Read the text with that in mind. |
| `RUN.AGENT.UNCERTAINTY_REPORTED` | Attention | The model said it was unsure about a specific part of the text. | Look at the place the model points to. |
| `RUN.SUBMIT.FAILED_CHECKS` | Attention | The model's last submission still fails the mandatory checks after the allowed repairs. | There is no accepted reading. The last attempt is shown for reference. |
| `RUN.SUBMIT.NONE` | Attention | The model never produced a submission. | There is no reading for this record. |
| `RUN.MODEL.REFUSAL` | Attention | The model refused to process the record. | There is no usable reading. Read the text. |
| `RUN.MODEL.ERROR` | Attention | A model call failed, or the session stopped on an error. | Attempts made before the error are kept and shown. |
| `RUN.MODEL.TRUNCATED` | Attention | A model response was cut off before it was complete. | The reading may be incomplete. |
| `RUN.AGENT.UNCERTAINTY_OVER_LIMIT` | Attention | The model reported more doubts than the allowed number. | The extra doubts were not recorded as readings but are still shown. |

## Settings behind the rules

- The model gets at most **14** calls per record, and **2** resubmissions after a failed mandatory check.
- The model may report at most **6** doubts per record.
- Two amounts count as equal when they differ by at most **0.005**; a tax amount agrees with base times rate within **0.011**; a calculation written in the text holds within **0.005**.
- In the shipment roll-up, an amount that is **1.03 to 1.07** times an earlier amount is treated as a restatement of it.
- A date in the text counts as "after the event" when it is more than **1** day(s) later than the event date.
- Text is checked for instruction-like wording with **12** patterns, and texts longer than **600** characters are flagged.

### Words accepted as a reason to leave an amount out

A dollar amount may be left out of the claim only if the words the model quotes contain one of these. Otherwise `NUM.JUDGMENT.EXCLUSION_BASIS_UNLISTED` is raised.

| Reason | Words |
|---|---|
| paid | PAID, PD, PAYMENT, PAYMENTS, PAYING, REMITTED, REMITTANCE, RECEIVED, SHORT PAID, SHORTPAID |
| billed | BILLED, INVOICED, INVOICE, CHARGED, REBILLED, RE-BILLED |
| total | TOTAL, SUBTOTAL, SUB-TOTAL, SUB TOTAL, BALANCE, AMOUNT DUE, SUM |
| unit rate | EACH, PER, RATE, @, /DAY, /HR, /HOUR, A DAY, AN HOUR, PER DIEM, AT |
| credit | CREDIT, CREDITED, CREDITS, REFUND, REFUNDED, OVERPAYMENT, OVERPAID, DEDUCT, DEDUCTED, DEDUCTION |
| history | PREVIOUSLY, PREVIOUS, PRIOR, EARLIER, ALREADY, ORIGINAL, ORIGINALLY |
| reference | APPROVED, APPROVAL, AUTHORIZED, AUTHORISED, QUOTED, QUOTE, AGREED, CONTRACT, CONTRACTED, TARIFF, ALLOWED, SHOULD BE |
